intro.text: An Alethi highprince fighting in the war on the Shattered Plains, and a political rival of Dalinar Kholin despite their old friendship.
An Alethi highprince on the Shattered Plains, named Highprince of Information by King Elhokar to investigate an attempt on the king's life.
An Alethi highprince who abandoned Dalinar Kholin's army at the Tower, believing Dalinar a threat to the kingdom, then traded his bridgemen for Dalinar's Shardblade.
An Alethi highprince and longtime enemy of the Kholins. He was murdered by Adolin Kholin shortly after arriving in Urithiru.

items.text: Sadeas was born in Alethkar into House Sadeas. At some point in his youth he became close friends with Gavilar and Dalinar Kholin.
House Sadeas was one of three princedoms that fought alongside the Kholins to unify Alethkar, and Sadeas and Gavilar plotted the war's strategy together.
Sadeas pushed the alliance toward greater brutality and was proud of his cruelty, hanging the heads of fallen highprinces and their officers and openly enjoying the pillage of conquered cities.

A persuasive politician, Sadeas won new allies with words, and dealt with those whose loyalty he doubted in quieter ways. His wife, Ialai, was known among their friends for devising elaborate schemes to remove troublesome allies and enemies.

After the unification, the city of Rathalas, the Rift, rose in rebellion under Tanalan. When Dalinar tried to negotiate a surrender, Tanalan offered to name the traitors who had helped him and accused Sadeas. Dalinar fell into a trap and realised it was Tanalan who had betrayed him. Finding that his army thought him dead, Dalinar agreed with Sadeas to delay word of his survival and to destroy the Rift entirely.

Sadeas remained a close ally of Gavilar. On the night of Gavilar's assassination, he acted as a decoy to lead the assassin away so the king could escape. Afterwards, he was the first highprince to pledge his support to King Elhokar when Elhokar called for war on the Parshendi to avenge his father.

Sadeas joined Dalinar, Adolin, Renarin and Elhokar on a chasmfiend hunt. When the beast emerged on the wrong plateau among the courtiers and scribes, Sadeas weakened it from a distance with his grandbow while the others attacked it. During the fight, Elhokar's saddle strap broke and threw him to the ground.
Sadeas and Dalinar worked together to manoeuvre Highprince Vamah into using more of the king's Soulcasters. Dalinar told Adolin that Sadeas had sworn to protect Elhokar at any cost.

At a feast, Elhokar announced that, after the attempt on his life with the saddle, he was naming Sadeas Highprince of Information to investigate. It was partly to spite Dalinar, whom the king thought was not taking the matter seriously, and Sadeas, who had heard that Dalinar wanted command of the war, used it to outmanoeuvre his rival.

Sadeas gave his findings publicly. Leatherworkers confirmed the strap had been cut, and he found that most of the gemstones powering the king's Shardplate had cracked, far more than a fall could explain, so someone must have sabotaged the Plate.

A groom testified that the saddle had been changed before the horse reached Dalinar's camp. To the shock of Dalinar and Adolin, who expected an accusation, Sadeas declared that the strap had been cut to cast suspicion on Dalinar and that Dalinar had no part in the plot. Despite their rivalry, he didn't want such an easy victory.

Right after being cleared, Dalinar proposed joint plateau assaults, combining Sadeas's speed with his own strength. Sadeas agreed once they had split the spoils: any Shardblades won would go to Sadeas, any Shardplate to Dalinar. The tactics worked in several battles, though once Dalinar had to rush to Sadeas's aid when the Parshendi sent an army straight at his banner.

Watching Adolin duel with Elhokar, Sadeas listened as Dalinar explained why he wanted to leave the war on the Plains. Sadeas asked to hear The Way of Kings sometime, and Dalinar agreed to use Sadeas's mobile bridges in their joint assaults.

When a chasmfiend was spotted on the Tower, a plateau where the Alethi had never won, Sadeas came to plan strategy with Dalinar, persuading him that the battle could cripple the Parshendi. Dalinar refused Sadeas's plan to send in all forty bridges in one wave, and would attack only after Sadeas had secured a landing point for his borrowed bridge crews.

At first the plan worked, and Sadeas carved out a landing for Dalinar. But when a second Parshendi force appeared behind Dalinar, Sadeas retreated to another plateau, taking with him the bridge crews he had lent and abandoning Dalinar and his army.
Back in camp, Sadeas told Navani with feigned regret that he had done all he could to save Dalinar, and vowed vengeance for his friend's death. Then a runner announced that Dalinar was approaching.

Sadeas offered a public apology, which Dalinar accepted. In private, Sadeas said he was keeping his oath to protect Elhokar and the kingdom: he feared Dalinar's talk of the Codes and of retreat was swaying the king, and he simply wanted Dalinar gone.

Dalinar asked for Bridge Four to fulfil a promise. Sadeas refused even a thousand broams a man, until Dalinar drove his Shardblade into the ground and offered it for every bridgeman in Sadeas's camp. Shocked, Sadeas agreed, gaining the Blade he had always wanted.

Sadeas found that owning Oathbringer didn't satisfy his thirst for bloodshed. He told Ialai that he meant to force the Alethi back into all-out war instead of chasing gemhearts, and had her send more spies into Dalinar's camp and prepare for further steps, including assassination.
To block Dalinar's plans, Sadeas made offers to Shardbearers who agreed to refuse Adolin's dueling challenges.

Sadeas undermined Dalinar and Elhokar by sending his fast bridge crews on plateau runs out of turn, beating the scheduled armies and throwing the gemhearts at their feet. Then he began claiming gemhearts had been lost while secretly keeping them.
Sadeas and Ialai watched Adolin's duel with Eranniv, spending it discussing their plots and Dalinar's attempts to unite the highprinces.
Waiting out a highstorm in a winehouse, Sadeas goaded Adolin about the Tower and how he meant to be rid of both Elhokar and Adolin. He wore uncut gems from a gemheart he had claimed was lost.

After Adolin won a duel against four Shardbearers, Sadeas had to accept his challenge, but slipped away before a time was set and accepted it for a year's time. He acted amused but was secretly terrified that Adolin was becoming another Blackthorn.

On a ride with Ialai to gauge the industry of Sebarial's warcamp, Sadeas argued against her idea of a coup, noting their last assassin had failed. Stunned to see Highprince Aladar join Dalinar's expedition, he decided it didn't matter: everyone on it would die, and he and Ialai should decide who would replace the doomed highprinces.
To general surprise, Sadeas answered Dalinar's call to the warcamps as quickly as Aladar and Roion, travelling to Urithiru with his wife.

While exploring the tower, Sadeas came upon Adolin alone and taunted him with the rumours he planned to spread about Dalinar. Adolin's restraint broke, and after a brief struggle he stabbed Sadeas through the eye with his side knife. He threw Oathbringer out of a window and hid the evidence.
Men of Bridge Four found the body, days after the death, and Sadeas's guards accused them of the murder. The death deepened the division between the camps, and many blamed Dalinar.
Soon afterwards Vedekar Perel was found dead with identical wounds.

Though some, like Sebarial, saw the death as one less problem for the alliance, Dalinar was deeply affected and asked Adolin to investigate. Struggling with guilt, Adolin confessed first to Shallan and then to Dalinar.

appearance.text: His Shardplate is painted red and decorated, with tassels on the helm.
A lighteyed man in his early fifties, with a bulbous head, curly hair and a ruddy face. His princedom's colours are green and white.

personality.text: He holds that the Codes, honour and compassion are weaknesses, and sees Gavilar's death as proof that the Codes lead to ruin.
Brutal and cruel, Sadeas has no compassion and enjoys showing off and pillaging. He sacrifices people easily to reach his goals, as with his bridgemen on the Shattered Plains.
A skilled politician and strategist, he shares a strong marriage with Ialai, who is just as good at intrigue. He enjoys authority but has no wish to be king, a job with little praise or amusement.
His professed aim is the stability of Alethkar, and he will sacrifice anyone he sees as a threat to it, even those he respects.
